NIELIT and Intel India Organized National Leadership Dialogue and Launched Agentic AI Skilling Programs for Preparing India’s Workforce for the Agentic AI Era
articles.full_content:
National Leadership Dialogue brings Government, Academia and Industry Together to Deliberate on Future Workforce Readiness; Agentic AI Skilling Program was Launched for the Skilling of Youth Across the Country
The National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, in collaboration with Intel India, organised a National Leadership Dialogue on “Preparing the Future Workforce for the Agentic AI Era” at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi.
The Dialogue brought together senior representatives from Government, foreign embassies, academia, industry and the skilling ecosystem to deliberate on the rapidly evolving Artificial Intelligence landscape and its implications for the future of work, education and workforce development in India.
The programme was attended by Shri Shashi Shekhar Vempati, Chairperson, Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) as the Chief Guest, Dr. M. M. Tripathi, Director General, NIELIT, Shri Sudeep Shrivastava, COO, IndiaAI Mission and Joint Secretary, MeitY, Mr. Anshul Sonak, Head & Global Director, Intel along with senior dignitaries and representatives from Government, academia and industry.
The Dialogue focused on the emerging opportunities and challenges presented by Agentic AI and the need to strengthen India’s workforce readiness for an increasingly AI-driven economy. Discussions centred around emerging skill requirements, industry-aligned curricula, experiential learning, faculty readiness, AI-enabled learning environments and stronger Government–academia–industry collaboration.
As AI evolves from predictive and generative systems towards Agentic AI-systems capable of reasoning, planning and executing complex tasks under human oversight-the skills required across industries are also evolving. The Dialogue highlighted the importance of preparing students, educators and professionals with the technical capabilities, adaptability and human-centric skills required to work effectively alongside increasingly capable AI systems.
Speaking at the occasion, Shri Shashi Shekhar Vempati, Chairperson, Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC), highlighted the importance of preparing India’s future workforce for the rapidly evolving Agentic AI era. He emphasized that skills, employability, and continuous learning will play a critical role as technology transforms the nature of work.
He congratulated NIELIT and Intel India for the initiative taken on democratizing Agentic AI.He further highlighted the need for long-term skilling pathways that combine foundational and emerging technology skills with real-world exposure, industry-relevant case studies and practical datasets. He also underscored the importance of sustained collaboration among Government, industry, academia and skilling institutions to ensure that India's youth are prepared not only for current employment opportunities but also for the jobs of the future.
Dr. Madan Mohan

A. Inflation expectations
• One year ahead business inflation expectation in July 2026, as estimated from the mean of individual probability distribution of unit cost increase, has marginally increased by 10 bps to 4.94%, from 4.84% reported in June 2026. The trajectory of one year ahead business inflation expectations of firms is presented in Chart 1.
• The uncertainty of business inflation expectations in July 2026, as captured by the square root of the average variance of the individual probability distribution of unit cost increase, remained elevated at over 2% for the past seven consecutive months.
Chart 1: One year ahead business inflation expectations (%)
• The cost perceptions data in July 2026 again indicates a mixed signal. The percentage of firms perceiving significant cost increase (in the range of 6% to 10%) has declined from 27% to 24%. However, the percentage of firms perceiving very significant cost increase (more than 10%) has remained in the range of 20-21%.
• At the same time, the percentage of firms perceiving costs ‘up moderately’ (over 3% but below 6%) in this round has increased to 26%, from 22% reported in the earlier round (Chart 2).

MNRE Hosts BRE Summit 2026 Roadshow in Ahmedabad, Spotlighting Gujarat as India's Renewable Energy Manufacturing Powerhouse
articles.full_content:

Building on the momentum generated in Jaipur, Mumbai and Hyderabad, leading voices from government, industry and the renewable energy sector gathered in Ahmedabad for the fourth in a series of regional roadshows for the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRE Summit) 2026, India's largest renewable energy summit and expo.
Hosted by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), the roadshow was organised in knowledge partnership with the National Solar Energy Federation of India (NSEFI) and supported by the Gujarat Federation of Solar Industries (GFSI). Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 will be held alongside the 9th Session of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) Assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen (ICGH), bringing together global leaders, policymakers, industry, investors and innovators on a common platform.
Delivering the keynote address, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Hon'ble Minister of State for Power and New and Renewable Energy, Government of India, said that " Gujarat has set an ambitious target of 105 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030, but what is most impressive is not any single number—it is the state's mindset. Where others saw constraints, Gujarat saw possibilities. Desert landscapes became solar parks, wind became an industrial opportunity, and today the state is leading the next frontiers of green hydrogen, energy storage, offshore wind, and clean energy manufacturing”.
He further highlighted The Bharat Renewable Energy Summit is designed to bring together policymakers, states, global investors, developers, technology providers, manufacturers, and financial institutions, creating a platform where policy meets capital, technology meets opportunity, and commitment moves towards implementation and invited Gujarat to participate in the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 in New Delhi with its projects, technologies, investment opportunities and ambitions, urging the state to play a leading role in shaping the next phase of India's clean energy future.
Shri Rushikesh Patel, Hon'ble Minister of Energy and Petrochemicals Department, Government of Gujarat, said that “ Our renewable energy journey is also deeply connected to our responsibility towards the environment and the generations that will follow us. We are already witnessing the consequences of environmental damage and rising temperatures. We are suffering now, and we must ensure that the next generation does not have to suffer. The effort to achieve this is in our hands, and it requires the participation of all of you. Our goal is clear, but we must also think about how we can m

IIT Roorkee Study Charts Scaling up Floating Solar Photovoltaic Systems to Support India’s Net Zero Goals
articles.full_content:
• Secretary, MNRE underscores FSPV as a new solar energy technology for India’s energy security along with optimal use of water resources • Study identifies recommendations for growth of FSPV in the country
In a significant contribution to India’s clean energy transition, the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee has prepared a comprehensive national-level report titled “ Scaling up Floating Solar Photovoltaic Systems (FSPV) ” , outlining recommendations to enable rapid development of FSPV in India in alignment with Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY) to support the country’s Net Zero 2070 goals.
These projects would provide an opportunity to gainfully utilize existing water reservoirs & industrial ponds, and eliminate competition for scarce land resources. FSPV will contribute to renewable energy capacity addition, support the achievement of national energy and climate objectives, and facilitate optimal utilisation of water resources while advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat.
The report was formally released by Shri Santosh Kumar Sarangi, Secretary, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) , who emphasized the importance of FSPV in India’s energy transition.
Shri Santosh Kumar Sarangi stated, “ Floating Solar PV systems will play an important role in enabling large-scale integration of renewable energy and optimizing the use of scarce water resources. As India accelerates towards its Net Zero targets, such evidence-based studies are essential to guide policy, investment, and implementation. This report provides valuable insights to strengthen our efforts towards building a resilient, reliable, and sustainable energy ecosystem. ”
Conducted under the leadership of Prof Arun Kumar, the study presents a comprehensive review of the global status, growth trends, and deployment of FPV systems, with particular emphasis on India. The study also reviews the policy and regulatory frameworks governing FPV development in various countries. Based on the findings of this international review, recommendations are proposed for the development of a robust and effective framework to support FPV deployment in India.
The key highlight of the study is the formulation of a strategy/ framework to support FSPV development in India. The recommended framework will facilitate the deployment of this technology, with key focus areas including site identification, environmental safeguards, and financial incentives.
Prof. Kamal Kishore Pant , Director, IIT Roorkee, in his foreword reflected IIT Roorkee’s commitment to advancing science-driven solutions for India’s clean energy transition. FSPV will play an important role in enabling scalable, and sustainable energy systems, not only supporting national priorities but also contributing to global climate and water conservation goals. ”

Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Chairs CEO Roundtable on Ease of Doing Business for Scaling India’s Data Centre Ecosystem
articles.full_content:
Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights USD 200 Billion Investment Potential in India’s Data Centre Industry Government Focuses on Ease of Doing Business to Accelerate India’s Data Centre Expansion Data Centre Roundtable Focuses on Reliable Power, Ready-to-Use Land and Streamlined Approvals
India is the world’s best location for setting up data centres, said Union Minister of Commerce & Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, at the CEO Roundtable on “Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) for Scaling India’s Data Centre Ecosystem” at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. While Chairing the meeting the Minister said the roundtable provided an engaging and fruitful platform for discussions with stakeholders from the data centre industry on further promoting the sector and enhancing ease of doing business in India.
Shri Goyal expressed confidence in India’s growth prospects amid global uncertainty and volatility and highlighted the country’s 7.8% growth in Q1. He complimented the people of India and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for his decisive leadership and for instilling confidence among every Indian to contribute towards Amrit Kaal and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
The Minister highlighted the potential of the data centre and semiconductor industries, India’s growing presence in AI and its expanding manufacturing base for global quality products, noting that these sectors would power India’s growth in the coming years and contribute towards achieving a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047. He said the interaction with stakeholders was marked by positivity and that discussions between different Departments of the Government of India and States had already helped resolve several issues. He said it was satisfying to see the industry geared up, with investments of around USD 200 billion potentially coming into the data centre industry. Shri Goyal said the meeting provided valuable insights and ideas on how India could become the data centre of the world.
The roundtable was convened as a follow-up to the inaugural CEO Roundtable to further strengthen the enabling ecosystem for the rapid and sustainable expansion of India’s data centre sector. Discussions focused on Ease of Doing Business and faster deployment of data centre infrastructure, particularly in the areas of power, land, regulatory and fiscal issues.
The discussions highlighted the rapidly increasing demand arising from cloud and Artificial Intelligence (AI) workloads. Hyperscalers accounted for more than 80 per cent of data centre absorption in the first half of 2026, underscoring India’s emergence as an AI infrastructure destination. The Government expects investments in the data centre sector to reach around USD 200 billion, reflecting the scale of the opportunity created by India’s rapidly growing digital economy and AI ecosystem.

Additional Information related to GDP Estimates Received After Release of Q1 Estimates of FY 2026-27
articles.full_content:
The Ministry has released the Updated Series of Annual and Quarterly GDP estimates with base year 2022-23 on 31 st August 2026. These GDP Estimates were updated using New Series of Output Producer Price Index (PPI); Banking Services Price Index (BkSPI) with the base year 2022-23 and updated data from various administrative sources.
The additional information being released now is mainly related to the adoption of double deflation methodology and consequent negative implicit deflators, its comparison with other deflation indices such as CPI and WPI, gap between nominal and real GVA/GDP, discrepancy between GDP estimates from production/income and expenditure side, comparison of new and old series growth rates, etc. To bring more clarity, the Ministry has brought out these additional questions and answers for the use of various stakeholders as per the Annexure .
Questions and Answers related to GDP estimates
• How can the manufacturing sector record a negative inflation in GVA implicit deflator of “-1.5%” in Q1, 2026-27 despite increase in both manufacturing output and input prices while the agricultural sector recorded a positive inflation rate of 3.9%?
A negative inflation in implicit deflator in manufacturing does not mean that manufacturing prices have fallen. It is important to distinguish between the price deflators of output and inputs and the implicit Gross Value Added (GVA) deflator .
Under the double-deflation approach, output and intermediate consumption of the manufacturing sector are deflated separately and real GVA is obtained as real output minus real intermediate consumption. Therefore, when input prices increase faster than output prices, the relative price movement can result in nominal GVA growing more slowly than real GVA. Consequently, the implicit GVA deflator , which is derived by comparing nominal GVA with real GVA, can show negative inflation even though both output and input prices are rising.
Importantly, a negative GVA deflator does not mechanically imply lower real growth. Real GVA growth depends on the relative movements in real output and real intermediate consumption.
An illustration to understand the above scenario is given below:

(PPI Output Index)
(PPI Input Index)

Deflated Inputs (Constant)
Real Value Added (Constant)

Constant Price Growth Rate (%)
As per illustration, nominal GVA grows by 12%, while real GVA grows by 17.5%, resulting in a negative implicit GVA deflator. This does not imply that the prices of manufactured products have fallen; rather, it reflects the relative movement of output and input prices under double deflation .

Ninth PM Vishwakarma marketing drive in Punjab brings AI tools to Bathinda artisans
articles.full_content:
The ninth in a series of PM Vishwakarma branding and marketing drives run across Punjab this year brought artificial intelligence tools to the traditional artisans of this district on Wednesday, a fortnight before the Centre's scheme completes three years of implementation on September 17th.
The day-long programme at Bathinda, in which artisans were taken through AI tools for product design, branding and marketing, drew 120 participants, among them 90 registered beneficiaries of the scheme and about 30 artisans of the district who have enrolled but are yet to complete registration. It was organised by the MSME Development and Facilitation Office, Ludhiana, along with the State Level Project Management Unit for the PM Vishwakarma scheme, under the Union Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.
Two facilitation desks ran through the day. India Post Payments Bank issued 15 QR codes for accepting digital payments, and staff of the District Industries Centre completed three fresh Udyam registrations at the venue. Fifteen of the 120 participants were women.
Artisans who obtained a QR code were able to accept payment digitally from a customer the same evening, without a further visit to any office and at no charge. Those registered under Udyam left with a formally recognised enterprise, a status that determines access to institutional credit and to public procurement.
The presence of artisans whose registration is still incomplete was by design. Officials said craftspeople at that stage are the most likely to drop out, having taken the first step without yet seeing a return, and both desks were opened to them on the same terms as to registered beneficiaries.
Eight sessions were held over the day. Apart from the AI session, which covered product photography, product descriptions, customer communication and hands on AI training, artisans were taken through labelling and packaging, pricing and costing, online selling and digital marketing, financial literacy and banking, the state government's support schemes, and central schemes including PMEGP, PMFME and MUDRA.
The costing session drew particular attention, dealing with a difficulty that persists across trades. Artisans working by hand routinely price their products without accounting for their own labour and end up selling below what the craft is worth.
The programme brought the MSME office, the PM Vishwakarma State Level Project Management Unit, Punjab, the District Industries Centre and India Post Payments Bank onto one platform. Private entrepreneurs also attended, allowing artisans to put questions on price, quality and order fulfilment directly to prospective buyers.
PM Vishwakarma, launched on September 17, 2023, covers artisans and craftspeople in 18 traditional trades. It offers recognition through a certificate and identity card, skill training with a stipend, a toolkit incentive, collateral free enterprise loans at a concessional rate, incentives for digital transactions and marketing
articles.summary: The ninth in a series of PM Vishwakarma branding and marketing drives run across Punjab this year brought artificial intelligence tools to the traditional artisans of this district on Wednesday, a fortnight before the Centre's scheme completes three years of implementation on September 17th. The day-long programme at Bathinda, in which artisans were taken through AI tools for product design, branding and marketing, drew 120 participants, among them 90 registered beneficiaries of the scheme and about 30 artisans of the district who have enrolled but are yet to complete registration. It was organised by the MSME Development and Facilitation Office, Ludhiana, along with the State Level Project Management Unit for the PM Vishwakarma scheme, under the Union Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

Understanding Q1 2026-27 GDP Estimates
articles.full_content:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Updated GDP Series
On 31 August 2026, the updated series of annual and quarterly GDP estimates with 2022-23 as the base year was released. The estimates incorporate the new Output Producer Price Index and Banking Services Price Index, both based on 2022-23, along with updated administrative data.
Two concepts are important in the latest GDP series: revision of the base year and adoption of double deflation for manufacturing.
Deflation removes the effect of price changes between two time periods from a current-price (nominal) value to get its value at constant prices (real value).
• The base year in National Accounts Statistics provides the reference prices used to calculate real growth. It is revised periodically to reflect structural changes and ensure relative prices remain representative of current economic conditions.
• The updated GDP series reflects an improved and more robust methodology. The double deflation method is adopted for various industries under the manufacturing sector. Under this, output and intermediate consumption are deflated separately to derive GVA at constant prices.
IMF describes double deflation as the preferred method for calculating GDP in volume terms.
To read more about India’s GDP Performance in Q1 2026-27, please refer to: India’s GDP Performance
To read more on India’s National Accounts Statistics revisions, please refer to: Counting What Counts: Strengthening India’s National Accounts and Core Economic Statistics
Deflation Methodology
• How can the manufacturing sector record a negative inflation in GVA implicit deflator of “-1.5%” in Q1, 2026-27 despite increase in both manufacturing output and input prices while the agricultural sector recorded a positive inflation rate of 3.9%?
Understanding Double Deflation: Under the double-deflation approach, output and intermediate consumption of the manufacturing sector are deflated separately. The real GVA is obtained as real output minus real intermediate consumption. Therefore, when input prices increase faster than output prices, the relative price movement can result in nominal GVA growing more slowly than real GVA.
Consequently, the implicit GVA deflator, which is derived by comparing nominal GVA with real GVA, can show negative inflation even though both output and input prices are rising.
Importantly, a negative GVA deflator does not mechanically imply lower real growth. Real GVA growth depends on the relative movements in real output and real intermediate consumption.
A negative inflation in implicit deflator in manufacturing does not mean that manufacturing prices have fallen. It is important to distinguish between the price deflators of output and inputs and the implicit Gross Value Added (GVA) deflator.

articles.full_content:
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Haryana Branch Office participated in the Vendor Development Programme (VDP) on EV Components, organised by MSME-DFO, Karnal, on 1–2 September 2026 at the ICAT Convention Centre 2, Manesar, Gurugram. The two-day programme brought together stakeholders from the MSME, automotive and electric vehicle (EV) ecosystem, providing a platform for interaction on business opportunities, technical requirements, government initiatives, testing, certification and regulatory aspects relevant to the rapidly growing EV component sector.
BIS Stall and Stakeholder Interaction A BIS stall was set up at the programme venue by the Haryana Branch Office in collaboration with Faridabad Branch Office. The stall received an encouraging response from participating industry representatives, stakeholders and visitors.
Relevant Indian Standards, research publications and reading material on EVs, including the National Electrical Code of India, were displayed at the BIS stall for the benefit of visitors. The BIS publication “EV Charging Infrastructure and Standards: An Overview” was also showcased to facilitate awareness of standards and safety requirements related to EV charging infrastructure.
The stall was visited by representatives from various industries and organisations, who interacted with BIS officials and showed keen interest in understanding the standards, certification and compliance requirements applicable to their products and operations.
Sh. Sanjeev Chawla, Additional Development Commissioner, MSME-DFO, Karnal, also visited the BIS stall along with his associates and colleagues. The interaction provided an opportunity to discuss the role of standards and conformity assessment in strengthening quality, competitiveness and market readiness among MSMEs, particularly those operating in the emerging EV component ecosystem.
Day 1 – Technical Sessions On 1 September 2026, BIS Haryana Branch Office contributed to the technical session on “Standards for EVs and Latest Developments in QCOs”, delivered by Sh. Saurabh Chandra, Scientist–D, BIS.
The session focused on creating awareness among MSMEs and other stakeholders regarding applicable Indian Standards, mandatory certification requirements and recent developments concerning Quality Control Orders (QCOs) for products relevant to the EV sector. The session also provided participants with an opportunity to seek clarifications regarding standards and certification requirements applicable to EV components and related products.

PM Vishwakarma Loan Utsav Held in Imphal East to Boost Credit Access for Artisans
articles.full_content:
The MSME Development & Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Imphal, Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India , along with the Lead District Bank Imphal East and SLBC , organised a Credit Outreach Camp under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme on September 2, 2026 , at the Training Hall, State Institute of Rural Development (SIRD), DC Office Complex, Porompat, Imphal East, Manipur .
The Credit Outreach Camp, organised as part of the Loan Utsav , aimed to facilitate access to institutional credit for PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries and provide on-the-spot assistance in addressing issues related to loan applications, sanction and disbursement. The initiative sought to promote entrepreneurship and strengthen the livelihoods of traditional artisans and craftspeople by improving access to institutional credit and other benefits available under the Scheme.
The programme commenced with a welcome address by Shri M. Siva Sai Reddy, Assistant Director, MSME Development & Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Imphal, Ministry of MSME, Government of India . He highlighted the key benefits available under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, including skill development training, modern toolkit support, marketing assistance, access to e-commerce platforms and subsidised credit facilities. He emphasised that these interventions can help artisans improve productivity, access wider markets and build sustainable livelihoods.
Shri Thakur Chandra Majhi, Lead District Manager, Imphal East , in his address, encouraged PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries to make full use of the Loan Utsav and available credit facilities under the Scheme to expand their enterprises and develop sustainable businesses.
Dedicated loan facilitation counters were set up by the participating banks to address credit-related queries of beneficiaries and facilitate the processing of loan proposals. The Camp also provided beneficiaries with an opportunity to interact directly with bank officials and seek clarification regarding loan applications, sanction and disbursement.
Around 100 PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries attended the Loan Utsav. The beneficiaries were sensitised on the importance of institutional credit in upgrading their enterprises, improving productivity and strengthening their socio-economic well-being.
A total of 15 banks participated in the Credit Outreach Camp, namely Bank of India, State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, IDBI Bank, Indian Bank, Axis Bank, Manipur State Cooperative Bank, Manipur Rural Bank, Punjab National Bank, HDFC Bank, IndusInd Bank, UCO Bank, ICICI Bank, Punjab & Sind Bank, and India Post Payments Bank . The participation of multiple banking institutions provided beneficiaries with direct access to formal financial services and enabled them to seek information and assistance regarding their credit requirements under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme.
The PM Vishwakarma Credit Outreach Camp provided a valuable platform to connect traditional artisans with institutional credit and banking

PM Vishwakarma Awareness workshop on Branding and Marketing held under MSME DFO Dimapur and District Industries Centre, Dimapur
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, through the MSME Development and Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Dimapur, in collaboration with the Department of Industries and Commerce and the District Industries Centre (DIC), Dimapur, organised a one-day Awareness Workshop on Branding and Marketing under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme at the Shilloi Lounge, Hotel Saramati, Dimapur on 2 September 2026. The programme was designed to strengthen the entrepreneurial capabilities of PM Vishwakarma artisans by equipping them with practical knowledge and technical insights on Product Packaging, Labelling and Design, Export Development, Artificial Intelligence, and Financial Literacy. The workshop witnessed participation from over 80 artisans from across the district.
The programme commenced with a welcome address by Smt N. Abeno Lotha, Functional Manager, DIC Dimapur, who encouraged participants to actively utilise the opportunities available under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme for enterprise growth and market expansion. This was followed by a keynote address from Shri Mohd. Ali Rahman, Director, MSME-DFO, Dimapur. He shared the progress status of PM Vishwakarma and the support provided by the scheme for artisans to sell their products on platforms such as Meesho and Amazon. He encouraged the artisans to take the workshops as an opportunity to showcase their work.
The first technical session on Product Packaging, Labelling and Design was delivered by Shri Imliakum, Founder of Nagaland Paper and Packaging. He spoke about the various types of packaging available, the suitability of packaging with products and how to communicate with customers through packaging.
A subsequent session on Export Development was conducted by Shri Kiyelu T Yeptho, Functional Manager, DIC Dimapur, who familiarised artisans with the fundamentals of export readiness. To engage the participants in understanding the concept of “money”, a hands-on session was conducted by Smt. Paweii Kayina, Founder of Moneybar. She spoke on different approaches to money, financial decisions and its intentional management.
This was followed by a brief from Smt. Talinaro Longchar, the Lead District Manager, SBI Dimapur, who interacted with the participants and addressed queries pertaining to credit facilities and loan applications. She also sanctioned loan letters to 8 PM Vishwakarma artisans.
A session on Business Development was delivered by Shri Thepfukedo Mere, Financial Analyst, RAMP Scheme, DIC Dimapur. He spoke on integrated business growth planning, financial management, and the importance of networking for enterprise sustainability and expansion. This was followed by a demonstration on QR code generation from Shri Rahul Suman and Mithun Kumar Biswas from the India Post Office, Dimapur to facilitate greater digital market access. An interactive session on Artificial Intelligence and e-commerce onboarding was subsequently conducted by the State Programme Management Unit

The programme was designed to strengthen the entrepreneurial capabilities of PM Vishwakarma artisans by equipping them with practical knowledge and technical insights on Product Packaging, Labelling and Design, Export Development, Artificial Intelligence, and Financial Literacy. The workshop witnessed participation from over 80 artisans from across the district.
